label.explanation: session-cache came back empty after a node replacement (line 224). With ~every lookup missing (lines 231, 235), account-svc sent its whole read load to accounts-db, saturating its connections and CPU (lines 232, 240, 249). The slow queries (lines 243, 256, 268, 288, 306, 308, 329, 349), account-svc query timeouts (lines 254, 267, 292, 314, 333) and edge-proxy 504s (lines 241, 248, 261, 265, 285, 293, 299, 310, 313, 332, 340, 350) are the cascade, not separate problems. Warm the cache / rate-limit fills. accounts-db is genuinely exhausted, so resource_exhaustion is defensible, but it was pushed there by the empty cache. Red herrings: line 205 (a single long GC pause in a healthy service, with heap well below limits); line 201 (a one-off slow reporting query on audit_log, not on the failing request path); line 57 (a routine disk usage warning on the log volume, nowhere near full); lines 52, 53 (a single identity provider connection reset that succeeded on retry, minutes before onset).
